thread:
sophie: Heads-up — planning a rolling maintenance for the us-west3 GPU burst pool next Tue 03:00-07:00 UTC. Goal: firmware micro-update plus cleanness pass on a subset of nodes, graceful drain so live requests fall back to the reserved pools.
ryan: timeline OK for me. what's the expected impact to latency/throughput during the window?
devon: we'll route new traffic to dedicated pools, but burst pool capacity will be reduced ~40% for the 4h window. expect transient queuing on large batches.
lina: can we pre-warm KV cache and bump burst pool to 1.15x 1h before to reduce pain?
sophie: yes — plan: (1) pre-warm prefix/KV cache 1h before, (2) scale burst pool up for 60m, (3) do cohorts of 10 nodes with graceful drain, (4) validate perf and roll next cohort.
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: MAINT-2026-330 (link: https://status.redwood.ai/maint/MAINT-2026-330) — watchers: #incidents, #support.
nate: checklist item — customer tiered routes: make sure production traffic for tier-enterprise stays pinned to dedicated for the whole window. who owns the route policy changes?
ryan: i'll own route policy and rollback hooks. will add a canary rule that pins 5% of traffic to a canary cohort for 30m post-drain.
lina: cost tradeoff note — scaling burst pool for 1h adds ~USD 3.8k. if we instead stagger longer but smaller cohorts we might reduce cost but increase maintenance time. prefer shorter pre-warm.
sophie: agree on shorter pre-warm. Add comms to customers — status note and targeted emails for enterprise. devon can you draft copy?
devon: yep. draft will include impact window, mitigation (dedicated routing), and rollback contact. will ping customer-success.
sophie: ops runbook snippet for drains (will paste to playbook):
```
# drain sequence
kubectl cordon node/$NODE
kubectl drain node/$NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
wait_for_empty_kv_cache $NODE || escalate
reboot_node $NODE && run post-reboot healthcheck
```
\nryan: also add a step to validate GPU cgroup reset and nvlink probe, sometimes we see lingering handles after soft reboot.
ops-bot: Reminder: add SLA guardrail: if error rates for prod > 1.5% for 10m, abort rollout and failover all traffic to dedicated.
lina: one more: who runs the rollback? we need a named oncall.
sophie: nate will be primary rollback, ryan secondary.
nate: ack. i'll be oncall Tue 02:30-08:00 UTC.
devon: putting comms draft in #product-comms for review; ops runbook pushed to /playbooks/maintenance/us-west3-burst.json.
sophie: perfect — i'll create the PagerDuty incident for the window and schedule a 15m preflight at 02:40 UTC. thanks all :thumbsup:
